recap_title: 🎯 Quick & Visual Recap: Laravel Mobile API Backend
recap_subtitle: Welcome, hero! This is a quick review supported by programming examples and illustrations for each session you learned in the course to help you remember the concepts with ease and fun and prepare for the super exam! 🚀🌟

points.title: Configured the development server and interpreter for PHP
points.desc: Installed a XAMPP server to run PHP, and used the VS Code editor to write scripts and understand the PHP tag structure.

points.title: Variables and printing in PHP
points.desc: How to reserve space in the program's memory to store texts and numbers and print them on the screen for the user.
points.code:
<?php
$userName = "Megaminds Hero";
$userAge = 14;
echo "You're welcome." $userName;
points.example: Display the student's welcome phrase on the browser screen.

points.title: Make software decisions (Logical If)
points.desc: Use logical comparison statements to execute specific codes only when the conditions specified in the program are met.

points.title: Check test scores
points.desc: Verifying the student’s score and directing him to wonderful, personalized win messages and incentives.
points.example: Dynamically change the status of the success and congratulations message.

points.title: Repeated code execution
points.desc: Using loops such as for and while to perform tasks repeated thousands of times at lightning speed and with very short code.

points.title: Countdown to the missile launch
points.desc: Simulating a countdown before a rocket launch to program games using a decreasing iteration loop.
points.example: Print individual numbers from 1 to 20 at a glance.

points.title: Building PHP Functions
points.desc: Grouping related codes into a specific function with a subname that can be called at any time to facilitate work and avoid code clutter.

points.title: Purchasing invoice calculation function
points.desc: A function that receives the original price of the item and the discount percentage and returns to us the final approved and discounted price.
points.example: Call the custom function to calculate the discount value for Magic Cake Shop.

points.title: Object-Oriented Programming (PHP OOP)
points.desc: A modern and universal programming style based on organizing codes around objects that simulate reality and facilitate the maintenance and development of programs.

points.title: Car object template design
points.desc: Define a class of cars with characteristics such as make and color, and create different cars and drive them programmatically.
points.example: Create a new user object for the student account in the database.

points.title: Data encapsulation and protection
points.desc: Protecting internal object data from random or malicious modification using software access controls such as security encapsulation.

points.title: Protecting the customer's bank balance
points.desc: Preventing direct modification of the customer’s bank balance and forcing the process to pass through smart and strict verification functions.
points.example: An excellent security application for withdrawing and depositing the financial balance.

points.title: Inheritance of software objects
points.desc: Inheriting general properties and functions from a parent class (Parent) to subclasses (Child) to prevent code duplication.

points.title: Programming animal objects
points.desc: Inherit the generic Animal class to create a Dog and Cat object while dynamically modifying the sound of each object to simulate polymorphism.
points.code:
class Animal { public function makeNoise() { return "Sound!"; } }
class Cat extends Animal { public function makeNoise() { return "Meow! 🐱"; } }
points.example: Designing permissions objects for the store manager and the regular buyer.

points.title: Interfaces and abstractions
points.desc: Building strict, abstract APIs that define the style and mandatory functions that other classes must implement to ensure the efficiency of the application architecture.

points.title: Electronic payment gateways application
points.desc: Forcing two payment gateways (Visa and PayPal) to provide a unified function for conducting transactions to facilitate changing the payment gateway in the future.
points.example: Connecting Visa payment gateways to mobile applications.

points.title: Relational databases (SQL & MySQL)
points.desc: Systems for storing and managing interconnected data in the form of programmed and tightly scheduled tables to serve millions of users.

points.title: Links and software keys
points.desc: Linking records between different tables using foreign keys to ensure integrity, consistency, and integrity of data.
points.example: Determine the buyer's unique identification number to link his invoices and purchases.

points.title: Database design standards
points.desc: Applying database organization and normalization rules to prevent data duplication and facilitate querying and periodic maintenance.

points.title: Design cake hangers and orders
points.desc: Link multiple cookies to multiple purchase orders for our customers by building an interactive and organized broker table.
points.example: Building a Pivot Table to store individual order items.

sessions.session_title: Session 11: Real Practice - Company Database Design

points.title: Building and planning a corporate database
points.desc: A practical application for designing a real database for a huge company that includes tables of employees, departments, and projects with full relationships.

points.title: Linking the employee to his administrative department
points.desc: Design a One-to-Many employee relationship to ensure easy employee management.
points.code:
//Department field in the Employee table
$table->foreignId('department_id')->constrained();
points.example: Determine the employee's financial department for easy extraction of payroll statements.

sessions.session_title: Session 12: Real Practice - Social Media Blog DB

points.title: Designing a database for a social networking application
points.desc: Database layout for a blogging or communication application that includes tables of users, articles, comments, and likes with professional accuracy.

points.title: Link comments to publishers' articles
points.desc: Design and implement an article-comment relationship to easily display readers' comments directly below the selected article.
points.example: Display interactive fan comments immediately below the published post.

points.title: Custom Laravel backend installation
points.desc: Download the framework and install it locally, activating the paths and tools provided for building lightweight and responsive programming interfaces.

points.title: API paths file for phones
points.desc: Use the api.php file to write backlinks to the application instead of web.php to direct them to mobile phones.
points.example: Request the link http://127.0.0.1:8000/api/health-check from the mobile application and confirm receipt of the response.

points.title: Mobile application interface controllers
points.desc: Create custom software controllers to process requests from smartphones and mobile applications with high efficiency and without blade templates.

points.title: Pass variables and return responses
points.desc: Receive the product ID number from the mobile application, search for it, and return its data in JSON text format.
points.example: The mobile application receives the complete chocolate cake data when its ID is requested.

points.title: Structuring and filling API tables
points.desc: Build the migrations programmatically and feed the tables locally with the processed data ready for developers and mobile applications to connect directly.

points.title: Run data seeds locally
points.desc: Filling the store with 30 types of cakes with images to facilitate previewing the shape and format of the mobile application during design.
points.code: php artisan migrate --seed
points.example: The mobile app screen is filled with delicious cake cards as soon as it connects to the back-end server.

points.title: Programming models and storing properties
points.desc: Customize forms and specify data filling characteristics and fields allowed to be shared with developers and mobile applications.

points.title: Protect users' sensitive data
points.desc: Hide passwords and sensitive security data programmatically and prevent them from appearing in JSON responses to phones.
points.example: Sending the buyer's account data to the mobile application while completely hiding the password for complete security.

sessions.session_title: Session 17: API Form Validation & JSON Errors

points.title: Verify and confirm data for phones
points.desc: Receives and validates registration requests from phones, returning JSON-formatted error messages instead of browser conversion.

points.title: Structured error responses in JSON
points.desc: Returns an array containing the exact error details for the mobile application so that the application displays it in a customized and smooth manner to the buyer.
points.example: Alert the mobile developer to write the email in the correct format to activate the save button.

sessions.session_title: Session 18: Eloquent CRUD API Database Actions

points.title: Perform data operations for API (CRUD)
points.desc: Programming the controllers to receive requests and complete the processes of saving, searching, updating and deleting the database directly from the phones.

points.title: Update the product price via the phone interface
points.desc: Receive the modification request with the new price values, save the changes, and notify the mobile application of the success of the process.
points.example: Save new store data and update it in a jiffy.

points.title: REST API design standards
points.desc: Use standard web request protocols and methods (GET, POST, PUT, DELETE) to clearly define the type of operation.

points.title: Standard API link format
points.desc: Organizing web server links to be uniform, understandable to all developers, and easy to use.
points.code:
GET /api/cakes // review
POST /api/cakes // Add new
DELETE /api/cakes/{id} // Delete a class
points.example: Link the mobile app's request to create a new account to the standard POST path.

points.title: Standard status codes for web responses
points.desc: Use HTTP numeric status codes to automatically inform a mobile application of the status of its request (success, error, unauthorized).

points.title: Returns the success code of adding the cake
points.desc: Returns the response in JSON format with standard status code 201 to confirm the save and the success of the operation.
points.example: The mobile application updates the interface immediately upon receiving success code 201.

points.title: Secure and protect the application interface server
points.desc: Cleaning and filtering phone user inputs and responding to suspicious requests to protect the server and database from any damage.

points.title: Filter and clean search fields
points.desc: Use the verification engine to filter out suspicious words and clean search terms before submitting them to the database.
points.code:
$cleanSearch = strip_tags($request->input('search_query'));
$results = Cake::where('name', 'like', '%'.$cleanSearch.'%')->get();
points.example: Protecting the mobile store's search engine against easy hacking attempts.

sessions.session_title: Session 22: Live Project API - Cake Store Backend

points.title: Build a magical cake shop backdrop
points.desc: Build and assemble end-to-end web server for cake shop to power smartphone applications with sales listings, buyer accounts and live bookings.

points.title: Cake reservation link to mobile application
points.desc: Create a dedicated POST link to receive cake reservation requests from phones, save them in the reservation table, and return the order number immediately.
points.code: Route::post('/order-cake', [OrderController::class, 'placeOrder']);
points.example: Confirm the order and notify the buyer of the reservation number immediately on his phone screen.

sessions.session_title: Session 23: Flutter App Integration - Connecting APIs

points.title: Configure the phone project to connect to the server
points.desc: Merge and connect step! Configure the mobile application built in Flutter to connect to the local Laravel API server and fetch data.

points.title: Call the cake review link in Flutter
points.desc: Program the code to retrieve data from the phone, ensure that the local server is accessible, and save the results.
points.code:
import 'package:http/http.dart' as http;
final response = await http.get(Uri.parse('http://10.0.2.2:8000/api/cakes'));
points.example: The Emulator successfully communicates with the local Laravel server.

sessions.session_title: Session 24: Flutter Live Data Rendering & Update

points.title: Showcasing live data and the culmination of the hybrid project
points.desc: The culmination of the double project! Converting the received JSON text data into amazing visual interactive programming cards on phone screens.

points.title: View reserved cake on phone
points.desc: Read the list of cakes from the API and draw excellent cards with images, names, and prices with the possibility of immediate interactive purchasing.
points.example: A complete cake shop application that runs on a smartphone and pulls all its data and images live from the Laravel backend server! 📱🌟
